38765.name: pip
38765.note: The pip package before 19.2 for Python allows Directory Traversal when a URL is given in an install command

38678.name: django-celery-results
38678.note: Django-celery-results through 1.2.1 stores task results in the database. Among the data it stores are the variables passed into the tasks.

39646.name: django
39646.note: Django 2.2.19 fixes a security issue in 2.2.18 (CVE-2021-23336).

40072.name: lxml
40072.note: The HTML cleaner in lxml 4.6.3 no longer includes the HTML5 'formaction' attribute to avoid it from allowing JavaScript to pass through.

40158.name: django
40158.note: Django 2.2.20 fixes a security issue with severity "low" in 2.2.19.

40163.name: django
40163.note: In Django 2.2 before 2.2.20, 3.0 before 3.0.14, and 3.1 before 3.1.8, MultiPartParser allowed directory traversal via uploaded files with suitably crafted file names. Built-in upload handlers were not affected by this vulnerability. See CVE-2021-28658.

40291.name: pip
40291.note: Pip 21.1 stops splitting on unicode separators in git references, which could be maliciously used to install a different revision on the repository.

40404.name: django
40404.note: In Django 2.2 before 2.2.21, 3.1 before 3.1.9, and 3.2 before 3.2.1, MultiPartParser, UploadedFile, and FieldFile allowed directory traversal via uploaded files with suitably crafted file names. See CVE-2021-31542.

40414.name: django
40414.note: In Django 2.2 before 2.2.22, 3.1 before 3.1.10, and 3.2 before 3.2.2 (with Python 3.9.5+), URLValidator does not prohibit newlines and tabs (unless the URLField form field is used). If an application uses values with newlines in an HTTP response, header injection can occur. Django itself is unaffected because HttpResponse prohibits newlines in HTTP headers.
